claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
Elevated-temperature chamber pre-heating during laser powder bed fusion will reduce thermal gradients in AlCrFeNiSi builds.
Reducing thermal gradients through pre-heating will reduce compositional segregation.
Reducing thermal gradients through pre-heating will reduce residual stresses.
Pre-heating will reduce processing-induced defect formation.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect formation will enhance mechanical integrity relative to room-temperature LPBF builds.
Elevating the chamber temperature decreases the temperature differential between the melt pool and its surroundings.
The lower temperature differential produces a slower cooling rate.
A slower cooling rate promotes more homogeneous solidification.
More homogeneous solidification suppresses compositional segregation.
Pre-heated builds will have a more uniform microstructure than room-temperature builds.
Pre-heated builds will exhibit enhanced yield strength relative to room-temperature LPBF builds.
Pre-heated builds will exhibit enhanced ductility relative to room-temperature LPBF builds.
Room-temperature LPBF of AlCrFeNiSi typically produces compositional segregation, high residual stresses, and comparatively high defect densities.
The proposed benefit is limited to pre-heating temperatures that do not trigger unexpected phase transformations or alter intrinsic material chemistry.
The intervention is expected to remain valid only for build sizes and geometries in which pre-heating uniformly moderates thermal gradients.
